title: Rendlesham Forest, December 1980
notes: Split from Appendix T's uk: the incident has its own witnesses and documents, and a reader looks for it by name.

lead.text: On nights between 26 and 28 December 1980, US Air Force personnel at RAF Woodbridge in Suffolk reported lights and an object in Rendlesham Forest; the deputy base commander, Lt Col Charles Halt, wrote it up in a memorandum describing a triangular metallic object and physical traces, and that memo remains the only contemporaneous US government document on the case.

summary.text: The events happened just outside RAF Woodbridge, which with Bentwaters was operated by the USAF's 81st Tactical Fighter Wing under NATO arrangements, and were reported up the chain by Halt.

The security police first responders on 26 December were James Penniston and John Burroughs; Halt led a forest patrol himself on 28 December. Their accounts differ in detail, which the board reads as a mark of independence.
Later claimants added to the case, notably Larry Warren, whose book with Peter Robbins was repudiated by Robbins and withdrawn by its publisher in 2017.

The British side of the record reached the public through the National Archives' release of MoD UFO files, the August 2009 tranche carrying the Rendlesham material, after an earlier release in 2001 pressed by the academic David Clarke.

record.text: Halt's memorandum of 13 January 1981, signed as Deputy Base Commander, describes an object metallic in appearance and triangular, about two to three metres across the base and two metres high, that lit the whole forest with a white light, and states that numerous individuals, including Halt himself, witnessed the activities it describes.

The memo records that on the day after the first sighting three depressions 1.5 inches deep and 7 inches across were found where the object had been seen on the ground, with beta/gamma readings of 0.1 milliroentgens peaking in the depressions and at the centre of the triangle they formed.
The Pentagon's FOIA office released the memo under case 97-F-1677 in September 1997, after earlier releases to other researchers.
The National Archives billed its August 2009 tranche, covering 1981 to 1996, as containing Britain's very own Roswell, Rendlesham Forest; the tranche's files include DEFE 24/1948.

The archive's catalogue records the papers of the earlier 2001 release under the heading of persistent correspondence from Dr David Clarke, the Sheffield Hallam academic who later served as spokesperson for the transfer of the MoD UFO files.
AARO's 2024 historical record report, Volume I, does not mention Rendlesham.

Warren's testimony is printed in the Disclosure Project's 2001 briefing document, dated September 2000, where he says he was assigned to the 81st Tactical Fighter Wing at Bentwaters and that his PRP clearance was approved on 11 December 1980; the board carries this as the dated fact of the testimony only.

claimed.text: Penniston says he touched the object and that it was warm and smooth with raised symbols on its surface; his contemporaneous notebook records the phrase craft of unknown origin.
Halt has stated in a notarised affidavit that the objects were under intelligent control and not of terrestrial origin, and that the US and UK governments acted to suppress the incident.

Burroughs says his service medical records for December 1980 to January 1981 could not be produced when he sought them for a VA claim; he was granted service-connected disability benefits in 2015 after congressional inquiries.
Warren, in his printed testimony, says he was a security specialist securing the nuclear weapons kept at Bentwaters and held a secret clearance.
Clifford Stone told the Disclosure Project that an Army team took him to Bentwaters in late December 1980.

One account holds that forty years on the American witnesses have kept to their stories, while the MoD's assessment of no defence significance was reached without interviewing them; the MoD desk officer who handled the file later spoke publicly for the first time about how it was processed.

contested.text: The UK Ministry of Defence's contemporaneous assessment was that the events were of no defence significance; one account says that assessment was reached without interviewing the American witnesses.
Burroughs himself says that on 26 December they followed the light for about 2 miles before they could see it was coming from a lighthouse, which cuts against a landed-craft reading of that night.

Warren's co-author of twenty-nine years, Peter Robbins, published a repudiation in June 2017 alleging a fabricated photograph with John Lennon, an altered medical card whose eye-injury notation he attributes to an orthopaedic surgeon, mismatched signatures, and testimonial letters that were never sent; the publisher suspended the book in October 2017, saying some experiences in it may be inaccurate or embellished.

Robbins concedes that Warren's January 1981 letter to his mother is authentic, and the paperwork he examined came from Warren himself, so what is disputed is Warren's presence at the events and the documents he produced for it, not his assignment to the base.
Halt is reported as saying Warren was not there, but this reaches the board only through search summaries and a video title, not a document by Halt, and is carried at Tier 3.

Stone's claim fails on his own act: according to Klass, in 1983 Stone filed a FOIA request to the USAF about the same incident from his home address without saying he was an Army sergeant, and the incident was not reported to higher officials until about two weeks after Stone says his team arrived.

The corroboration the Disclosure Project offers for Warren is internal to its own document: on the board's reading, two of the three named corroborators are witnesses in the same briefing, one of them Stone, and nothing opened places Warren at its 2001 press conference.
Robbins describes himself as no longer interested in researching the case, and the documents he describes were not opened by the board.

questions: The MoD judged the events of no defence significance, and astronomers have attributed parts of the 26 December sighting to a fireball and the Orfordness lighthouse; Halt rejects both. Was any American witness ever interviewed by the MoD?
Is there any released document that supports Halt's later assertion that witnesses were drugged and hypnotically debriefed?
Does any record support Penniston's binary-code account, which surfaced about two decades after the incident?
Is there a document written or signed by Halt on whether Warren was present, and what do Warren's own service record and duty roster show?
What do the medical card, in-processing sheet and letters Robbins describes actually show, and what did the sceptic Ian Ridpath find?
On what basis did the VA grant Burroughs's claim, and where are his missing medical records?
Why does AARO's historical review leave out a case whose commander's memo the Pentagon itself released?
